1.overview: John presents the revelation as a message from God through Jesus Christ and an angel, introduces Jesus’ titles and coming, and addresses the seven churches of Asia. On Patmos, John sees the risen Christ among seven lampstands, receives a command to write, and learns that the stars and lampstands represent the churches’ angels and the churches.

sections.heading: John’s Vision of the Risen Christ

2.overview: The risen Christ addresses Ephesus, Smyrna, Pergamum, and Thyatira, commending their deeds and endurance while identifying failures involving lost love, coming persecution, false teaching, and tolerance of Jezebel. He calls the churches to repentance or perseverance and promises the tree of life, protection from the second death, hidden manna and a new name, and authority over the nations with the morning star.

3.overview: Christ addresses Sardis, warning that its reputation for life masks spiritual death, calling it to wake, remember, and repent, and promising white garments and names retained in the Book of Life to the faithful. He commends Philadelphia for keeping his word and promises protection and honor, then condemns Laodicea’s lukewarmness and self-sufficiency, calling it to repent and promising fellowship and a place on his throne to the one who overcomes.

4.overview: John is called through an open door into heaven, where he sees the throne, the twenty-four elders, and four living creatures amid signs of divine power. The creatures proclaim the holiness of the Lord God Almighty, and the elders worship the enthroned One, casting down their crowns and declaring that all things exist by his will.

5.overview: John sees a sealed scroll in the hand of the One on the throne, and an elder identifies the triumphant Lion of Judah, the Root of David, as worthy to open it. The slain Lamb takes the scroll, and the living creatures, elders, angels, and all creation praise the Lamb and the One on the throne.

sections.heading: The Sealed Scroll and the Worthy One
Praise from Heaven and All Creation

6.overview: The Lamb opens the first four seals, revealing horsemen associated with conquest, the removal of peace, scarcity, and death across the earth. At the fifth seal, slain witnesses call for justice and are told to wait; at the sixth, cosmic upheaval drives people of every rank to hide from the wrath of the One on the throne and the Lamb.

7.overview: John sees four angels hold back the winds until God’s servants are sealed, and he hears the number of the sealed from Israel’s tribes. He then sees an uncountable multitude from every nation worshiping before the throne and the Lamb, and an elder identifies them as those who come through the great tribulation and receive God’s care.

8.overview: When the Lamb opens the seventh seal, silence falls in heaven as an angel presents the prayers of the saints before God and casts altar fire to earth. Seven angels prepare their trumpets, and the first four bring judgments on the earth, sea, waters, and heavenly lights before an eagle announces three woes for the remaining blasts.

sections.heading: The Seventh Seal and the Altar

9.overview: At the fifth trumpet, a star opens the Abyss, releasing locusts that torment those without God’s seal for five months under the rule of Abaddon, or Apollyon. At the sixth trumpet, four angels bound at the Euphrates lead a vast mounted force that kills a third of humanity, while the survivors persist in idolatry and other sins.

sections.heading: The Four Angels and the Mounted Force

10.overview: John sees a mighty angel standing over sea and land, hears seven thunders whose words he is forbidden to write, and hears the angel swear that God’s mystery will be fulfilled when the seventh angel sounds. At heaven’s command, John takes and eats the angel’s open scroll, which tastes sweet but turns bitter, and receives a commission to prophesy again about many peoples, nations, languages, and kings.

sections.heading: The Angel and the Seven Thunders

11.overview: John is told to measure God’s temple while the nations trample the holy city, and the two witnesses prophesy, are killed by the beast, and are raised and taken to heaven. At the seventh trumpet, heavenly voices announce the Lord and Christ’s reign, the elders proclaim judgment and reward, and the heavenly temple opens with the ark visible.

sections.heading: The Temple and Holy City Measured
The Two Witnesses and Their Vindication
The Seventh Trumpet and Heavenly Reign

12.overview: A woman gives birth to a son destined to rule the nations, while a dragon seeks to destroy him; the child is taken to God’s throne, and the woman finds refuge in the wilderness. Michael and his angels drive the dragon, identified as the devil and Satan, from heaven, and a heavenly voice declares the Lamb’s victory before the dragon pursues the woman and makes war on her other children.

sections.heading: The Woman, the Child, and the Dragon
War in Heaven and the Dragon’s Defeat

13.overview: A beast rises from the sea, receives authority from the dragon, and is worshiped as it blasphemes God and wages war against the saints. A second beast rises from the earth, deceives the earth’s inhabitants into worshiping the first beast and its image, and imposes a mark associated with buying and selling and the number 666.

sections.heading: The Beast’s Authority and the Saints

14.overview: The Lamb stands on Mount Zion with the 144,000, who sing a new song and are described as redeemed and blameless. Three angels announce judgment and warn against worshiping the beast, while a heavenly voice blesses the dead who die in the Lord; the chapter closes with images of the earth’s harvest and the winepress of God’s wrath.

15.overview: John sees seven angels carrying the final plagues and the victors over the beast standing beside a glassy sea, singing of God’s mighty works, holiness, and just ways. The heavenly temple opens, the angels receive golden bowls of God’s wrath, and smoke fills the temple until the plagues are completed.

16.overview: A voice from the temple sends seven angels to pour out God’s bowls of wrath, bringing sores, blood, scorching heat, darkness, and judgments that prompt curses but no repentance. The sixth bowl dries the Euphrates and gathers the kings at Armageddon through demonic spirits, while the seventh brings a great earthquake, Babylon’s judgment, and devastating hail.

sections.heading: The Seventh Bowl and Final Plagues

17.overview: One of the seven bowl angels shows John the great prostitute, identified as Babylon the Great, seated on a scarlet beast and drunk with the blood of the saints. The angel interprets the beast, its seven heads and ten horns, and the woman, describing the kings’ war against the Lamb, their destruction of the prostitute, and her identity as the great city ruling the earth’s kings.

18.overview: A glorious angel declares Babylon fallen, and a voice from heaven calls God’s people out of the city while announcing judgment for its sins. Kings, merchants, and seafarers mourn Babylon’s destruction, while heaven and the saints are called to rejoice as an angel depicts the city’s irreversible fall and blood guilt.

19.overview: Heavenly voices praise God for judging the great prostitute and announce the Almighty’s reign and the Lamb’s marriage; an angel tells John to worship God. Heaven opens to reveal the rider called Faithful and True and the Word of God, who defeats the beast, the false prophet, and the assembled kings and armies.

sections.heading: The Lamb’s Marriage and the Angel
The Rider Called Faithful and True
The Beast and Its Armies Defeated

20.overview: An angel binds Satan in the Abyss for a thousand years, while those who remained faithful to Jesus come to life and reign with Christ. After Satan’s release, his forces are destroyed and he is thrown into the lake of fire; the dead then stand before the great white throne and are judged, and Death and Hades are also cast into the lake of fire.

21.overview: John sees a new heaven and a new earth, the New Jerusalem descending from God, and hears that God dwells with his people, ends death and sorrow, and gives life and inheritance to those who overcome while the wicked face the second death. An angel shows John the city’s dimensions, gates, foundations, and precious materials, while God and the Lamb serve as its temple and light, and only those in the Lamb’s Book of Life enter.

sections.heading: The New Creation and Its People
The City’s Light and Its People

22.overview: The angel shows John the river of life and the tree of life in the city, where God’s servants see his face and reign without curse or night. The angel and Jesus affirm the prophecy, announce Christ’s coming and reward, warn against altering the book, and close with an invitation to the water of life, John’s prayer, and a blessing.

sections.heading: The River and Tree of Life
The Angel’s Words and John’s Response
